prompt: Explain the concept of encapsulation in object-oriented programming. NEGATIVE CONSTRAINT 1: Do not use the words 'data', 'hide', or 'class'. NEGATIVE CONSTRAINT 2: Format the output as a Markdown table with two columns: 'Concept' and 'Description'.
evaluation_criteria:
Negative Constraints: 0-5 (Evaluates avoidance of forbidden words)
Markdown Table: 0-5 (Evaluates precise table formatting)
response_text:
### Encapsulation Concept
| Concept | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Bundling | This involves combining multiple elements into a single unit, making it easier to manage and maintain. |
| Abstraction | It is the practice of exposing only the necessary information to the outside world, while keeping the internal details private. |
| Access Control | This refers to the ability to control how other parts of the program interact with an object's internal state, ensuring that it is modified only in a controlled manner. |
| Information Concealment | The internal implementation details of an object are not directly accessible from outside, reducing the risk of unintended modifications. |
| Modularization | Encapsulation promotes modular code, where each object is a self-contained module with its own internal state and behavior, making it easier to update or replace without affecting other parts of the program. |
